## 1. Signed webhook
The AIOps worker posts every incident here. The **Webhook** node checks the HS256 token against the *AIOps webhook signature* credential (signature, expiry); **Verify signed payload** checks that the token was issued for this exact payload, notification and incident. Invalid requests get 400, valid ones 202 before anything is sent.

## 2. Claim, route, send
The engine is asked first: a notification can be claimed once, so a repeated webhook never sends twice. A critical alert pages on-call with sound at once, before any analysis; the analysis follows silently, as a reply to the page. Other critical or warning alerts (resolved, flapping) are sent silently; info is recorded only. Telegram calls are retried 3 times, 5 s apart.

## 3. Report back
Every outcome (delivered with Telegram's message ID, failed with the reason, suppressed) goes back to the engine, which stores it with the incident and measures the time from alert to message.
